review_summary: The junior differential captures the major organ systems involved but several probabilities are mis‑scaled and important high‑impact entities (type 2 MI, acute‑on‑CKD, cardiorenal syndrome) are omitted. Evidence for sepsis and plasma‑cell dyscrasia is lacking. Adjusted probabilities reflect the dominance of ACS and advanced CKD, elevate the likelihood of euglycaemic ketoacidosis, and downgrade unsupported items. Additional labs and imaging are required to confirm several secondary diagnoses.
